candidates.attacker_control: Indirect: PushBuilder.path() is called by application code, but deployments commonly derive the pushed path from request data (query parameters, route segments naming images/scripts to push). The defect triggers whenever the path contains two or more consecutive percent-encoded octets, i.e. any non-ASCII character or adjacent encoded characters.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Pushed requests still traverse the normal authenticator and security-constraint pipeline as the same authenticated user, and pushed responses go to the client that initiated the push, which limits impact. The same loop may be long-standing upstream code (no pristine copy available to diff), in which case it is a latent correctness bug rather than the benchmark's targeted vulnerability. No stronger concrete defect was found in auth, rewrite, multipart, webresources, or request-parsing code; the published mid-2025 hardening items are present in the snapshot.
candidates.impact: Lossy/corrupt decoding of pushed request paths (embedded NUL and dropped bytes), so pushed requests can be mapped/resolved differently than the application intended and inconsistently with the path presented in the PUSH_PROMISE. Where the container makes mapping/constraint decisions from the corrupted decoded path while the application validated the original path, this is a container-vs-application path inconsistency; I did not confirm unauthorized access, data disclosure, or code execution.
candidates.prerequisites: HTTP/2 push usable and an application that calls request.newPushBuilder()/PushBuilder.path() with a path containing >=2 consecutive %nn sequences, ideally influenced by request input.
candidates.root_cause: In ApplicationPushBuilder.decodePercentSequence, the byte array is sized one element per percent-triple (sequence.length()/3) but the loop advances i by 3, indexing bytes[i], while reading source characters at offsets 1 + 3*i and 2 + 3*i. As written, i is used simultaneously as a byte index and as a triple index, so only every third triple is decoded for sequences with two or more consecutive %nn triples (bytes 1..n-1 stay 0x00). The caller decode() deliberately groups all consecutive %nn triples into a single call, so any multi-triple sequence (e.g. UTF-8 %C3%A9, or two adjacent encoded octets) is decoded into a string containing NUL bytes and dropped characters.
candidates.title: Incorrect loop increment in HTTP/2 PushBuilder percent-decoding corrupts pushed request decoded paths
candidates.trace: path(p) stores the path (line 172) and push() (line 289) sets pushTarget.requestURI() from pushPath (line 341) and pushTarget.decodedURI() from decode(pushPath, charset) (line 342); decode() (line 369) groups consecutive %nn and calls decodePercentSequence() (line 398), which fills the byte array incorrectly. Because the pushed request URI is a String (MessageBytes.T_STR), CoyoteAdapter.postParseRequest takes the else branch (lines 653-667) and trusts req.decodedURI() as 'the decoded, normalized form' used by Mapper.map for servlet mapping and by RealmBase.findSecurityConstraints/StandardContextValve for constraint and /WEB-INF checks, while the PUSH_PROMISE :path remains the original encoded path.
candidates.unverified: Runtime mapping behavior and the exact consequences of a corrupt decoded URI were not tested. Whether an attacker-influenced push path can turn this into a privilege or authorization bypass was not demonstrated. Whether this code differs from upstream Tomcat (injected/reverted fix vs. long-standing upstream defect) is unresolved.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-193 Off-by-one / incorrect decoding of encoded input (CWE-20 adjacent)

coverage_summary: Files were enumerated via the source-scope tool (3,031 visible files; no file-count exclusions, no symlinks, no >5 MiB files, no sensitive-name exclusions; binary-like files are refused). I read and traced the areas most relevant to remotely reachable vulnerabilities: java/org/apache/catalina/connector (CoyoteAdapter, Request, Response), authenticator/*, realm/* (RealmBase constraint/permission logic), valves (RewriteValve, RemoteIpValve, RequestFilterValve, ParameterLimitValve, ProxyErrorReportValve), filters (CorsFilter), servlets (DefaultServlet, WebdavServlet, CGIServlet, SSI), core (ApplicationPushBuilder, ApplicationContext, NamingContextListener), webresources (DirResourceSet, StandardRoot, FileResource, WebResourceLockSet), util (UDecoder, RequestUtil.stripPathParams/normalize, URLEncoder, Escape, HexUtils, ContextName), Coyote HTTP/1.1 (Http11Processor input-filter arbitration, Http11InputBuffer) and parts of HTTP/2, multipart (FileUploadBase, MultipartStream, FileItemIteratorImpl), session (StandardSession/Store persistence), jakarta/el ImportHandler, and the bundled webapps JSPs/servlets I considered highest risk. I did not exhaustively read every one of the ~2,600 Java files; Jasper/JSP compiler internals, most of WebSocket, Tribes/membership, naming, dbcp/jdbc-pool, and large parts of the documentation and example webapps were only spot-checked.
limitations: No git metadata/history is present, so I could not diff this snapshot against upstream Tomcat or against the presumed fix commit; conclusions about whether code is genuine upstream vs. altered are inferential.
The test tree is absent, so no regression tests, expected outputs, or failure information could be used to localize the defect, and no code was executed or built.

The repository version was inferred from webapps/docs/changelog.xml (10.1.42 in development), MERGE.txt (2025-06-05), and .github/workflows/ci.yml (JDK 24); build.properties.default is absent so the exact build number could not be confirmed.
I could not retrieve or verify any CVE/advisory text in this environment; the CVE-2025-49125 hypothesis is based only on recollection and is not source-evidenced.
The submitted candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability: its runtime mapping consequences and exploitability were not demonstrated, and its divergence from upstream code is unverified.

rejected_leads.lead: Preemptive-authentication bypass in AuthenticatorBase/BasicAuthenticator (possibly the CVE-2025-49125 timeframe fix, since the snapshot is a 10.1.42-dev branch state and the multipart maxPartCount/maxPartHeaderSize hardening is already present)
rejected_leads.reason: Traced AuthenticatorBase.invoke, all four isPreemptiveAuthPossible overrides and their doAuthenticate methods, checkForCachedAuthentication, register, logout, FormAuthenticator (matchRequest/saveRequest/restoreRequest), SingleSignOn and RequestFilterValve. In every path I traced, a protected resource forces authRequired via hasAuthConstraint and hasResourcePermission still applies role checks; I could not exhibit a concrete bypass, so I did not claim one.

rejected_leads.lead: RequestFilterValve.denyRequest (lines 382-392) forwards a denied request to the next valve when invalidAuthenticationWhenDeny=true and the context has preemptiveAuthentication=true, without overwriting a pre-existing Authorization header
rejected_leads.reason: Behavior is explicitly documented ('An already existing authentication header will not be overwritten', webapps/docs/config/valve.xml) and appears to be by design; exploitation also requires the attacker to hold valid credentials. Not submitted as a vulnerability.

Only used when no CA certificate is configured (configureCaCert logs a warning and the InsecureStreamProvider class name/doc make the trade-off explicit); appears to be intended upstream behavior for cloud membership, and the endpoint URL is administrator-configured.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultServlet.renderHtml inserts directoryWebappPath (and the parent path) into <title>/<h1>/anchor text without Escape.htmlElementContent (lines 1823, 1831, 1852), while entry names are escaped (line 1938)
rejected_leads.reason: A directory name containing HTML would be required on the file system (write-enabled WebDAV/PUT or application-created directory), and the unescaped pattern appears to be long-standing upstream code; impact and divergence from upstream could not be established.

rejected_leads.lead: ParameterLimitValve stores URL patterns in a ConcurrentHashMap and applies the first matching entry (lines 92, 264-275)
rejected_leads.reason: Iteration order is unspecified, so overlapping patterns can apply a nondeterministic limit; this is configuration-dependent hardening weakness with no demonstrated privilege/impact.

summary: Snapshot reviewed: Apache Tomcat 10.1.x, changelog section "10.1.42 (in development)" with 10.1.41 "release in progress" and MERGE.txt recording the Commons FileUpload 1.6.0-RC1 merge dated 2025-06-05 (i.e. ~mid-June 2025 branch state). I traced the main attacker-facing paths: HTTP/1.1 request parsing (Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding arbitration), CoyoteAdapter URI/path-parameter decoding/normalization, authentication (AuthenticatorBase, Basic/Digest/Form/Spnego/SSL, SingleSignOn, RequestFilterValve and the documented preemptiveAuthentication / invalidAuthenticationWhenDeny interaction), rewrite valve encoding, DefaultServlet (range/partial PUT limits, HTTP/2 push), webresources/write locking, multipart limits (Connector maxPartCount=10 / maxPartHeaderSize=512, Request.parseParts, FileUploadBase, MultipartStream), session persistence, EL import handling, TrustManager usage, and the manager/WebDAV servlets. Known mid-2025 hardening (maxPartCount/maxPartHeaderSize, partial-PUT range checks, canonical-cache protections, RemoteIpValve IPv6 internal proxies, %nn rewrite encoding) is present in the code, so I could not attribute a missing published fix. The single strongest concrete source defect I could substantiate is an incorrect percent-decoding loop in the HTTP/2 PushBuilder path handling (details below). I could not confirm an exploitable authentication/authorization bypass, and I explicitly do not claim one.
